description: Admin screens for Solhigson apps as Razor components, rendered on the server. An app owns its routes; the package ships no page.
releaseNotes: 10.4.0: the audit trail screens (Solhigson.Admin.Components, Solhigson.Admin.Auditing). The reader seam: IKitAuditReader, which AddSolhigsonAdmin registers scoped over the framework's IAuditTrailReader<TContext> for the context it is given, as it registers IKitAudit, is how the audit screens read the audit trail (Available; SearchAsync of a KitAuditSearch, answering a KitAuditPage of KitAuditRow; GetAsync of a record's id and created key, answering a KitAuditLookup of a KitAuditRecord; each answer carrying a KitAuditOutcome, Done, NotAvailable, ActorRefused, NotFound or Failed, and KitAuditMessages.For's sentence). It refuses a viewer who is not signed in before anything is read, reads the time once from the registered TimeProvider and resolves one window from the viewer's days in their zone through the framework's AuditTrailWindow, passes every filter and the cursor, answers NotAvailable with no query when no reader resolves or the context does not map AuditTrail, and throws nothing but the caller's cancellation; a fault's line names the filters set, never their values. A row's Linkable, ActorLinkable and ActorAttempted say whether a link may carry its entity id or its actor id, so text a sign-in caller typed never reaches a link, and a name a caller gave on a security event is marked as attempted. People are named for the viewer: a name a row stores shows to every viewer; an id it stores with no name is looked up in one UserAdministration.ResolveDisplayNamesAsync call a page or a record, and shows as the user's name only when the viewer's scope admits the user, else as a fragment of the id; a subject is looked up only on a user's entity type under an allow-listed action, KitAuditOptions' UserEntityTypes (User by default, beside the identity's own user class) and ResolvedSubjectActions (the users.* actions by default); a record about a user the viewer may not reach is Restricted and carries no changes, no snapshot and no address, a record's address is withheld unless the lookup names its actor for the viewer, while a record with no actor id keeps its address, which ShowIp shows to every viewer unless the record is Restricted, and a failed lookup sets NamesUnavailable. With no user-administration rules registered nothing is looked up or restricted, so the audit page's permission belongs only to roles that may see every user. KitAuditLabels gives the package's 15 audit actions a label and a verb phrase (For, Sentence, TypeInWords), so a record reads "Ada Obi changed the roles of Jane Doe", and any other action reads as the framework's AuditDisplay labels it; KitAuditEvent.SettingEntityType names the settings screen's entity type. The audit list: KitAuditList, which an app places on its own page with DetailHref (holding {id} and {created}) and an optional TimeZone, lists the records of one window newest first, a page at a time: the header says the window in the viewer's zone, with Today, Last 7 days and Last 30 days; a GET filter bar holds the days and the category, and behind More filters the action, the subject type, the subject id and the person (the query names from, to, category, action, type, id, actor and cursor), each matched exactly as stored; the table shows when, what (the action's label, linking to the record), the subject and the person, a subject linking to its history and a person to their activity only where the row allows it; a search naming a subject or a person and no day reads all time. The audit entry page: KitAuditDetail, on a page with the record's id and created key in its route, taking Id, Created, ListHref, an optional UserHref and TimeZone, and ShowIp (false unless set), shows one record: its sentence as the title, when it was written in the viewer's zone, the facts (the category, the action, the subject, the person, the source and, with ShowIp, the address), What changed and Recorded values, a masked value reading Hidden and a payload not in the stored shape shown as text in a block that scrolls inside itself; nothing in a record is ever markup; a record not found answers 404, and the page must not stream. The history links: KitSettingsEditor, KitUserDetail and KitRoleDetail gain HistoryHref, the audit page's path, with which each setting's row ends with a History link, the user page's header gains History and Activity by this person, and the role page's header gains History, kept after a delete, each to the audit list with no day; a HistoryHref that KitHref.Local refuses, or that holds ? or #, throws before any read, and with none set nothing renders. To adopt: add two pages (the audit list, a record by id and created key), each with its route and [Permission]; the record page must not stream; map AuditTrail in the context passed to AddSolhigsonAdmin; the audit trail is one trail for the whole app, so the permission decides who reads it; a name is looked up only for users the viewer's scope admits, while a name stored on a record shows to every viewer; a record about a user the viewer may not reach shows no values; an app that captures its user class adds "securitystamp" to AuditCaptureOptions.AdditionalSensitiveNamePatterns, through a pre-populated AuditCaptureOptions singleton the framework's registration leaves in place, since the defaults do not mask SecurityStamp, which the record page would show ("securitystamp" masks the secret and nothing else, where a plain "stamp" would also mask any Timestamp column); rows captured before the pattern keep the raw stamp, so an app that has captured its user class adds the pattern, then rotates every user's security stamp (UserManager.UpdateSecurityStampAsync) before it grants the audit permission, which ends every open session at the next stamp check; an app never opts Identity's user-token, user-login or user-claim types into capture, since their values are credentials no pattern masks and their records are not restricted; add any other user class name, beside the identity's own, to KitAuditOptions.UserEntityTypes and its own safe user actions to ResolvedSubjectActions; pass TimeZone; ShowIp is off by default; pass HistoryHref to the settings, user and role pages. The README lists each log line the reader seam writes (KitAuditReaderNoActor, KitAuditReaderSearchFailed, KitAuditReaderGetFailed, KitAuditReaderUnresolved) and each line the screens' reads cause under AuditTrailReader, UserAdministration and the users seam, its level and what to do; the screens write no line of their own. The kit: KitNotice, given a KitNoticeMessage (KitNoticeMessage.Landed or NotLanded, a blank text or step throwing), says a post's answer in one message at the foot of the screen that rises in, stays (--kit-notice-dwell, --kit-notice-long-dwell) and leaves on its own, in CSS alone, and is drawn only inside KitShell, which tells it to a screen reader through two live regions that kit.notice.js fills; KitButton gains Answer (KitButtonAnswer: None, Landed, a ring in the success colour, or Failed, a sideways nudge), drawn on the render that answers a post, changing neither the button's colour, text nor size, and still under reduced motion; kit.forms.js removes every notice and both answer classes as it marks a post's submitter busy, so the next answer plays; KitFilterBar gains Enhance, true unless set, false for a bar holding a field named after a form's own member, such as action, which then submits as a plain form; kit-facts is the facts list the audit record page and the user page share; kit.manifest.json gains the kit-audit, kit-facts and kit-notice names, the kit-btn-landed, kit-btn-nudged, kit-gallery-notices, kit-role-history and kit-user-history classes, the component token --kit-audit-raw-height (the raw payload block's height, the measure unless set) and the tokens --kit-d-flash, --kit-flash-spread, --kit-flash-ring, --kit-flash-ring-end, --kit-d-nudge, --kit-nudge-1, --kit-nudge-2, --kit-nudge-3, --kit-d-notice, --kit-d-notice-leave, --kit-notice-rise, --kit-notice-dwell, --kit-notice-long-dwell, --kit-z-skip and --kit-z-float, and loses none; every new duration token is 0ms under reduced motion. Changes for a 10.3.0 app: AddSolhigsonAdmin also registers IKitAuditReader and, when the app registers no TimeProvider, TimeProvider.System, each kept when the app registered it first; KitHead also links kit.notice.js, with the page's nonce as its other scripts; KitShell renders two empty, visually hidden live regions, a status and an alert, after its main region on every page; the user page's facts list also carries the kit-facts class, its kit-user-facts class kept; and the header line of the user and role pages, and of the new-user and new-role screens, is a flex row that wraps, spaced by its gap, so a back link after a wrapped email or group takes its own line. Minor bump: every type and member is new but for those changes. Depends on Solhigson.Framework.Core 10.29.0 or later. 10.3.0: the role and permission screens (Solhigson.Admin.Components, Solhigson.Admin.Roles). The roles seam: IKitRoles, which AddSolhigsonAdmin registers scoped over the framework's RoleAdministration as it registers IKitUsers, is how the role screens read and change roles (ListAsync, GetAsync, HeldPermissionsAsync, OfferedPermissionsAsync, SetPermissionsAsync, RemoveGrantsOutsideOfferAsync, CreateAsync, DeleteAsync, PermissionsAsync, GroupNamesAsync; with KitRolePage, KitRoleLookup, KitRoleRow, KitHeldPermissions, KitOfferedPermissions, KitPermissionPage, KitRoleResult and KitRoleAudit's roles.* actions, GroupNamesAsync answering the 10.2.0 KitRoleNames); it reads the acting user by the users seam's rule, adds no rule of its own and throws nothing but the caller's cancellation. KitRoleLinks.For builds every link to a role from the app's template, and a role's page passes its route value as given, never decoded again. The roles list: KitRolesList, which an app places on its own page with DetailHref (holding {name}) and an optional CreateHref and UsersHref (holding {role}), lists every stored role by group, then name, with a GET filter by group: the name linking to the role's page, marked Yours or View only, the group, the users holding it in every tenant with a link to the ones the viewer manages, and its grants. The role page: KitRoleDetail, on a page with the role's name in its route, taking RoleName, ListHref, an optional UsersHref and CanManage, says first whether the viewer can change the role and why not, then shows what the role holds, the grants its group offers by top permission and those outside the offer with their class in words, and how many users hold it; a role not found answers 404, and the page must not stream. With CanManage, for a role the viewer may edit and does not hold: the permission editor, one form with a box for each permission the role's group offers, a box disabled where the viewer may not give the permission and the role does not hold it, so a viewer adds only permissions it holds unless the app's rules answer its Grant with All, saving through SetPermissionsAsync, refused as stale when the role's grants changed since the page loaded, and recorded as roles.permissions-changed; the clearing of out-of-group grants, a confirm that removes the grants the group may not hold that the framework marks removable (HeldPermission.Removable), recorded as roles.outside-grants-removed; and delete, a confirm opened only while no user in any tenant holds the role, answered RoleInUse otherwise, removing the role and its grants, recorded as roles.deleted. A save, a removal or a delete answered Failed may have been stored: the page reads the role again and says what it found, and no audit row is written. A post carries two values for each permission the role holds, so FormOptions.ValueCountLimit (1024 unless the app sets it) bounds a save at about 500 held grants, a longer post answered 400 with nothing saved. Role creation: KitRoleCreate, with ListHref, DetailHref and CanCreate (false unless set), creates a role holding no permission, its name of at most 64 characters, in the stored group the viewer chooses, where the app's rules' MayCreateRoleAsync allows it, which refuses unless the app writes it; it records roles.created and links to the new role's page, or says that an administrator who may grant the role must set its permissions, or that its group is not declared; a Failed create says the role may have been created, so look it up before creating it again. The permissions list: KitPermissionsList, with an optional RoleHref, lists every stored permission in the role editor's order, with its parent, the groups its declaration allows (a Warn pill for one offered to no group) and the roles holding it, with a GET search and, with permission groups registered, an offered-to-no-group filter. The role page and the new-role page refuse framing: the app sends X-Frame-Options: DENY and Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none' on them, and the components set no header. A deleted role's name can be created again, and that role then gets the seed's AllowedRoles grants that its group may hold and matches any open session still carrying the role claim until its stamp is next checked; a role the app seeds leaves the seed before it is deleted. The README lists each log line the role screens write (the seam's KitRolesNoActor and KitRolesFailed, the guard's KitUserSeamAuditFailed and KitUserSeamDoneUnnamed, the audit seam's, and the framework's lines under RoleAdministration and Solhigson.Framework.PermissionGroups that the screens cause), its level and what to do, beside the role_administration counter on the meter Solhigson.Framework.Identity. The kit: KitButton gains BusyText, the doing word a submit button reads with three working dots while its post is out, and kit.forms.js now holds a form whose kit button is busy, so a second submit of it is not sent until the answer is on the page or --kit-btn-busy-dwell (20s) passes; a theme pick cross-fades the colours (--kit-d-theme, --kit-d-theme-hold); a page change inside KitShell slides in from the side it came from (kit.nav.js and kit.core.js, which KitHead links with the page's nonce; --kit-d-enter); the rail's marker glides to the current item where the browser can anchor it (--kit-d-glide); every such motion stops under reduced motion; kit.manifest.json gains the kit-role, kit-roles, kit-permissions, kit-enter, kit-rail-marker and kit-theme-fading names and the new tokens, and loses none. Changes for a 10.2.0 app: an audit seam that throws now writes KitUserSeamAuditFailed (event id 3), naming the event's entity type and id, in place of KitUserSeamFailed (event id 2), so an alert on the old line stops seeing audit throws; AddSolhigsonAdmin also registers IKitRoles, kept when the app registered it first; a # in the users list's DetailHref now ends its path as a ? does; and the email change's limits no longer offer gating a reset on a confirmed address, since whoever reads the new address can confirm it through a confirmation sent without the user's sign-in (the anonymous ResendEmailConfirmation page of Identity's default UI) or an external sign-in matching accounts by address: where the app's sign-in sends a reset to an address it has not confirmed, only keeping AllowEmailChange off guards an address takeover, so an app that relied on that gate turns AllowEmailChange off. Minor bump: every type and member is new but for those changes. Depends on Solhigson.Framework.Core 10.29.0 or later. 10.2.0: the user screens (Solhigson.Admin.Components, Solhigson.Admin.Users, Solhigson.Admin.Auditing). The users list: KitUsersList, which an app places on its own page with DetailHref (holding {id}), an optional CreateHref and a TimeZone, lists the users within the signed-in user's reach a page at a time: the name linking to the user's page with the email under it, the roles, the status (Disabled a Neutral pill, Locked out a Warn pill, No password plain text), two-factor and the last sign-in; GET filters by role, status, two-factor, no password and not signed in for 30, 90 or 180 days; and a posted search over email and user name whose text never reaches a link, a form's action, a header or the address. The user page: KitUserDetail, on a page with the user's id in its route, taking UserId, ListHref, TimeZone, CanManageAccess and CanConfigure, says first whether the user can sign in and why not, then shows Access, Two-factor (when the app registers it) and Roles; a user missing and one out of reach both answer 404, and the page must not stream. Its actions each act on the route's id alone, are refused for the viewer's own account and without their permission (a post then gets 400), are recorded through IKitAudit, and say in one alert what was done and what did not follow: with CanManageAccess, Enable, and Disable after a KitConfirm; End lockout; Send password link, for a user with no password; and Reset two-factor after a KitConfirm, which removes the authenticator and the password; with CanConfigure, the roles form, offering the roles the viewer may grant and those held, refused as stale when the roles changed since the page loaded, and saying when RoleChangeDisables makes a save disable the user; and, where the app turns on UserAdministrationOptions.AllowEmailChange, Change email, refused for a user who holds a role the viewer may not grant, the new address starting unconfirmed. User creation: KitUserCreate, with ListHref, DetailHref, CanCreate and an optional ExtraFields fragment for the app's own fields, creates a user with an email, a phone and the roles the viewer may grant, with no password and disabled while NewUserStartsDisabled is on, and asks for a password link; the user is built by the app's IKitUserFactory<TUser> (KitUserBuild.Of or KitUserBuild.Refused), else through the user type's public parameterless constructor, and an app whose rules scope users by tenant must register a factory that sets it, or every create answers NotFound. The seams: IKitUsers, which AddSolhigsonAdmin registers scoped over the framework's UserAdministration, is how the screens read and change users (SearchAsync, GetAsync, GrantableRolesAsync, RoleNamesAsync, SetEnabledAsync, UnlockAsync, ResetTwoFactorAsync, SetRolesAsync, ChangeEmailAsync, CreateAsync, TwoFactorAvailable, SignInNeedsConfirmedEmail; with KitUserSearch, KitUserPage, KitUserLookup, KitUserRow, KitRoleNames, KitUserResult, KitNewUser, KitUserMessages and KitUserAudit's users.* actions), and throws nothing but the caller's cancellation; IKitSessions (Ends, EndAsync) and IKitUserNotices (PasswordLinkNeededAsync, AccessChangedAsync, TwoFactorResetAsync, EmailChangedAsync), which an app registers to end sessions in its own store and to send the link and the notices, and whose defaults answer false and warn once a process, so the screens tell the administrator what to send and how long an open session lasts, read from the security stamp validation interval and the application cookie; and IKitUserFactory<TUser>. One rule names the acting user for the users seam and the audit seam alike: the first claim of Identity's ClaimsIdentity.UserIdClaimType, counted only from a signed-in identity. Changes for a 10.1.0 app: the audit seam's actor, when the actor provider gives the unattributed one, now follows that rule, so the sub fallback is gone and an app whose tokens carry the id as sub sets UserIdClaimType to sub; AddSolhigsonAdmin now also registers IKitUsers, so it registers IKitMenuSource, IKitAudit, IHttpContextAccessor and IKitUsers, each kept when the app registered it first; KitAuditEvent's payload holds no personal value but users.email-changed's previous address; and KitAuditFailed names the exception's type only, never its message. KitHref.LocalOrThrow gains an overload taking what the value must be (KitHref.MustPost, KitHref.MustLink), KitPageHeader gains LineContent, KitFilterBar gains Id, and kit.manifest.json gains the kit-user and kit-users names. The README lists each log line the screens and seams write, its level and what to do, beside the framework's user_administration and two_factor counters on the meter Solhigson.Framework.Identity. The user pages refuse framing, as the settings page does: the app sends X-Frame-Options: DENY and Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none' on them, and the components set no header. With AllowEmailChange on, one administrator holding both CanConfigure and CanManageAccess can take over any account within reach whose roles they may grant: move its address, then send a password link or reset its two-factor. Where the app's own sign-in sends a password reset to an address it has not confirmed, the address change alone is enough for a user without two-factor, needing CanConfigure only; a user enrolled in two-factor still needs the second factor after the reset while the app's two-factor is on, and CanManageAccess as well removes that limit, since the two-factor reset removes the factor. Only keeping AllowEmailChange off guards that path. Giving the two permissions to different roles does not, and neither does a reset that asks for a confirmed address: an email change leaves the new address unconfirmed, but whoever reads it can confirm it through a confirmation the app sends without the user's own sign-in (Identity's default UI has an anonymous ResendEmailConfirmation page), or through an external sign-in that matches accounts by address. Where the app's sign-in sends no password reset by email and no external sign-in matches accounts by address, an app guards by giving the two permissions to different roles. Registering IKitUserNotices tells the previous address, after the fact. Minor bump: every type and member is new but for those four changes. Depends on Solhigson.Framework.Core 10.27.0 or later. 10.1.0: the settings screen, the package's first screen (Solhigson.Admin.Components, Solhigson.Admin.Settings, Solhigson.Admin.Auditing). KitSettingsEditor, which an app places on a page of its own with its route and [Permission], lists every setting the app's catalogue declares, one section a group in the order the catalogue registered them, under a Settings header that counts them and links to a needs-attention view, with a GET filter over key, name and purpose, never a value. CanEdit, false unless set, comes from a second permission: without it no form renders, a post is the framework's 400 and a Personal value shows as Hidden; a Secret's value is never written into the page. With it each line is a form of its own that saves or resets that setting through Core's SaveDeclaredSettingAsync and ResetDeclaredSettingAsync and says the outcome at the line: saved, reset, no change, a refusal beside the field in the screen's words with what was typed kept (never a secret's), changed since the page loaded, failed with no exception text, and a Warn alert when other instances were not told and may show the old value until their settings cache recovers. Under the groups, Rows with no declaration lists each stored row no declared setting matches, by name and flag pills, never a value; with CanEdit each has a Remove that opens one KitConfirm saying older code may still read the row by name and the screen cannot put it back, and its confirm calls RemoveUndeclaredRowAsync. Above the groups a warning says a secret's save is refused while the legacy encryptor is in force. The setting field: KitSettingField renders one KitSetting (KitSetting.From(DeclaredSettingLine)) with one control of its kind: a Switch a toggle that submits its form when it changes (a Save in noscript otherwise), a number with min, max and step, a Duration an amount and a unit or one text field, a List a textarea, a Text a text field; a Secret, a row stored sensitive and a masked line an empty password field, with no value or mask in the markup; with ReadOnly, Fields, Error and ChildContent. KitSettingValue.Compose turns the posted KitSettingFields into the setting's stored text or a refusal sentence (KitSettingComposed), never an exception, and Fill gives each control's starting values. The audit seam: IKitAudit (Records, and RecordAsync answering whether a row was written), which AddSolhigsonAdmin registers scoped as KitAudit<TContext>, resolving the audit service, the actor provider and the context from the request at first use; KitAuditEvent and KitAuditActions. Each save, reset and removal done is recorded as a SecurityEvent on AppSetting, settings.saved, settings.reset or settings.stray-removed, with the actor and a payload of the key and the values before and after as the framework's result shows them, the mask for a Secret, a row stored sensitive and a Personal value. A removed stray row stored plain under a plain name keeps its raw value in the append-only audit row: only a row stored sensitive or under a secret-looking name is masked. When Records is false (no audit service resolves, or the context maps no AuditTrail and no IAuditSink is registered) the screen says changes here leave no audit record and one Warning is logged a process; a record that fails logs one Error and says so at the line, and the change is not undone. TContext must be registered scoped. KitConfirm gains OnConfirm and KitDialog OnSubmit, so a confirm's form is handled by the component that owns it; kit.forms.js submits the form of a data-kit-submit-on-change control and keeps one such post in flight a page; the gallery gains a settings section; kit.manifest.json gains the kit-setting and kit-settings names. The README documents the app's page and every log line the screen, the seam and a save write. Minor bump: every type and member is new, and no existing component's behaviour changes. Depends on Solhigson.Framework.Core 10.27.0 or later. 10.0.0: the first release of Solhigson.Admin, the admin kit: Razor components for Solhigson apps, rendered statically on the server, with no interactive render mode and no inline script; an app owns every route, and the package holds components and no screen yet. Head and theme: KitHead, first in <head>, links the kit's stylesheet and scripts with the page's nonce where its policy uses one; KitTheme reads the viewer's light or dark choice from its cookie on the server, with KitTheme.HtmlAttributes(HttpContext) for <html>, and KitThemeSwitch offers the choice. Components: KitButton, KitStatusPill and KitAlert; KitField, one field for every input kind; KitDialog (a modal or a drawer) and KitConfirm on the native <dialog>; KitMenu, KitMenuItem and KitMenuForm, a row menu on the native popover; KitShell, the admin layout with a skip link, a side rail, a top bar with the user's menu (the theme choices and sign-out) and the main region; KitPageHeader, KitLead, KitEmptyState and KitPager; KitTable with KitColumn, and KitFilterBar, Get or Post; KitMark; and KitGallery, every component in every state on fixed example data, for a page an app adds in development or behind a permission. Links: every url a kit component takes goes through KitHref: a ~/ path is joined to the path base; a button's or a link menu item's Href may also be an https:// address (KitHref.LocalOrHttps), and a form's action is local alone (KitHref.Local). Menu: IKitMenuSource builds the shell's menu from the permissions the signed-in user's roles hold, read through PermissionManager's cached reads, and AddSolhigsonAdmin<TUser, TContext>() or AddSolhigsonAdmin<TUser, TKey, TContext>() registers it; the menu shows, each page's [Permission] enforces. Styles: tokens for every colour, size, space, radius, shadow, duration, curve and font, light and dark, in layers (kit.tokens, kit.base, kit.components) that an app's app layer overrides, each name listed in kit.manifest.json, a name leaving which is a breaking change; every motion reads a duration token that is 0ms under prefers-reduced-motion. Rules: the package's tests hold its markup, scripts and stylesheets to no inline script, style or handler, no other host, every href and form action through KitHref, measured contrast pairs, and no colour, length or duration outside the tokens. Depends on Solhigson.Framework.Core 10.24.0 or later.
